is_anopheles.evidence: The study monitors and profiles insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. malaria vectors (An. gambiae s.s., An. coluzzii, and An. arabiensis) in Guinea-Bissau (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes Vgsc L1014F (L995F), L1014S (L995S), N1575Y (N1570Y), and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) (Section 2.5, Page 2; Table 3, Page 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 on Page 4 reports mutant allele frequencies with sample sizes (number of alleles) for L1014F, L1014S, N1575Y, and G119S across multiple populations.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae/pupae from field sites in Buba, Gabu, Bafatá, and Bissau in Guinea-Bissau in October 2018 (Section 2.2, Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original bioassay and molecular genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were performed at specific sentinel regions: Buba, Gabu, Bafatá, Cacheu, and Bissau (Section 2.2, Page 2; Fig. 1, Page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Fieldwork was conducted from 6 to 31 October 2018 (Section 2.2, Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes routine surveillance and collections funded by the Global Fund and INFRAVEC2, with no indication of sample overlap with other published datasets.

supplement.evidence: All primary target marker frequencies, sample sizes, and bioassay results are fully reported in the main text tables (Tables 1, 2, and 3).

assessment.summary: This study monitors insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations across five regions of Guinea-Bissau in October 2018. It reports high frequencies of the Vgsc L1014F mutation, the first detection of the N1575Y mutation, and low frequencies of the Ace-1 G119S mutation, alongside WHO tube bioassays demonstrating pyrethroid resistance.
